question: In a distribution where the empirical relation holds true, if both the mode and the median are 46, find the mean.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Empirical formula: Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

Given Mode = 46, Median = 46

⇒ 46 = 3×46 − 2Mean

⇒ 46 = 138 − 2Mean

⇒ 2Mean = 92 ⇒ Mean = 46

**∴ Answer = 46**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode = 46, Median = 46

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ 46 = 3(46) − 2Mean

⇒ 46 = 138 − 2Mean

⇒ 2Mean = 92

⇒ Mean = 46

**∴ The correct answer is 46.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

Mode = 3Median − 2Mean

Special Case

If Mode = Median ⇒ Mean = same value

Key Insight

All three measures become equal
